title: SCAPI | B2C Commerce API
snippet: The B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) is a set of RESTful APIs for building storefronts, merchant tools, and integrations on the B2C Commerce platform. It also goes by “Salesforce Commerce API” or just “Commerce API.” For B2C Commerce customers, the API is available at no extra cost.

title: Add an API Client in B2C Commerce
snippet:
Account administrators can use Account Manager to create API clients. To access the Salesforce Commerce API (Shopper Commerce API (SCAPI)) or Open Commerce API (OCAPI), you must use an API client. Append the API client ID to the URLs that you use to access these APIs. An API client is also required to use the On-Demand Sandbox API.
You can't use the same client ID for both the B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) and OCAPI. Each API framework requires its own client ID. An API Client ID that's meant for OCAPI must *not* have the role "Salesforce Commerce API" assigned to it.

- **Confidential**: Suitable for applications that run on servers or platforms capable of securely storing a client secret.
- **Public**: Suitable for environments where a secret cannot be hidden, such as single-page web apps or native mobile and desktop applications. Uses Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) to exchange OAuth tokens securely. For public API clients, you cannot assign a role, set a password, or use a JWT public key.

title: Agentic B2C Developer Toolkit
snippet:
For SCAPI administrative commands, create an [Account Manager API client](/docs/commerce/commerce-solutions/guide/authorization-for-admin-apis.html). In Account Manager, assign the client the **Salesforce Commerce API** role, select each instance that the client needs to access through SCAPI, and add the scopes required by the task. For example, listing eCDN zones requires the `sfcc.cdn-zones` scope.

`--tenant-id` accepts a tenant ID such as `abcd_stg` or its organization ID, `f_ecom_abcd_stg`. The CLI requests the access token for the command; you don’t need to obtain or paste a bearer token first.
SLAS client administration uses the **SLAS Organization Administrator** role. Managed Runtime commands that use an API key accept `MRT_API_KEY`, available from [Runtime Admin Account Settings](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/account/settings). Cartridge and WebDAV operations can also require an instance hostname, username, and WebDAV access key, depending on the authentication method.

title: Development Environment Setup
snippet: For SCAPI job execution, configure your Account Manager API client with the **Salesforce Commerce API** role for the instance and the `sfcc.jobs` and `sfcc.jobs.rw` scopes. Supply the instance hostname, short code, and tenant ID in your [B2C CLI configuration](/docs/commerce/commerce-vibes/guide/b2c-developer-tooling.html#configuration-and-authentication). Listing apps across all sites also requires site-discovery access (`sfcc.sites`). WebDAV access is still required for archive uploads and downloads.

title: Salesforce Commerce Cloud API Essentials
snippet:
### 1. Sign up for a Salesforce Developer Account
First, you need to create a Salesforce Developer Account if you don't already have one:
1. Go to the Salesforce Developer website (developer.salesforce.com).
2. Click on the "Sign Up" button.
3. Fill out the registration form with your details.
4. Verify your email address.
### 2. Access B2C Commerce
Once you have a Salesforce Developer Account, you'll need to get access to B2C Commerce:
1. Contact Salesforce sales or your account representative to request access to B2C Commerce.
2. They will provide you with the necessary credentials and access to a B2C Commerce instance.
### 3. Set up your B2C Commerce instance
After getting access to B2C Commerce:
1. Log in to your B2C Commerce Business Manager.
2. Navigate to Administration > Site Development > Salesforce Commerce API Settings.
3. Request a short code if you haven't used the B2C Commerce API in your realm before.
4. Note down your organization ID, realm ID, and instance ID.
